question:
(a) Given A = {-5, -3, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3}, B = {-4, -3, 0, 3, 5, 8}. Find A Δ B.

(b) If A, B, and C are any sets, show that A ∪ (B ∪ C) = (A ∪ B) ∪ C.

(c) In an election involving three parties for the chairmanship and gubernatorial election of Lagos State, voters cast their votes as follows: 190 voted for party A, 200 for party B and 250 for party C. 80 voted for A and B, 60 voted for A and C, 100 voted for B and C and 40 voted for B alone. If 500 people voted during the election, find:
(i) The number of voters who voted for all the three parties.
(ii) The number of voters who voted for A and B but not C.
(iii) The number of voters who did not vote for any party.
modelAnswer:
(a) A Δ B = (A - B) ∪ (B - A)
A ∩ B = {-3, 0, 3}
A - B = {-5, -1, 1, 2}
B - A = {-4, 5, 8}
A Δ B = {-5, -4, -1, 1, 2, 5, 8}

(b) Forward: Let x ∈ A ∪ (B ∪ C).
If x ∈ A, then x ∈ A ∪ B, so x ∈ (A ∪ B) ∪ C.
If x ∈ B ∪ C, then x ∈ B or x ∈ C.
If x ∈ B, then x ∈ A ∪ B, so x ∈ (A ∪ B) ∪ C.
If x ∈ C, then x ∈ (A ∪ B) ∪ C.

Backward: Let x ∈ (A ∪ B) ∪ C.
If x ∈ C, then x ∈ B ∪ C, so x ∈ A ∪ (B ∪ C).
If x ∈ A ∪ B, then x ∈ A or x ∈ B.
If x ∈ A, then x ∈ A ∪ (B ∪ C).
If x ∈ B, then x ∈ B ∪ C, so x ∈ A ∪ (B ∪ C).

Therefore A ∪ (B ∪ C) = (A ∪ B) ∪ C.

(c) Let x = number who voted for all three parties.
|B only| = |B| - |A ∩ B| - |B ∩ C| + |A ∩ B ∩ C|
40 = 200 - 80 - 100 + x
x = 20

(i) 20 voters voted for all three parties.

(ii) |A ∩ B only| = |A ∩ B| - |A ∩ B ∩ C| = 80 - 20 = 60

(iii) |A ∪ B ∪ C| = 190 + 200 + 250 - 80 - 60 - 100 + 20 = 420
Did not vote = 500 - 420 = 80

question:
(a) In the study of motion of rigid bodies, explain the following concepts:
(i) Moment of inertia of the system
(ii) Radius of gyration of the system

(b) Find the moment of inertia and radius of gyration of a uniform thin rod of length 2a, density ρ about an axis passing through one end of the rod perpendicular to its length.
modelAnswer:
(a)(i) Moment of inertia (I) is the sum of products of each particle's mass and the square of its perpendicular distance from the axis:
I = Σmᵢrᵢ² or I = ∫r² dm
It resists angular acceleration: τ = Iα. SI unit: kg m².

(a)(ii) Radius of gyration (k) is the distance from the axis at which the entire mass M could be concentrated and still have the same moment of inertia:
I = Mk² → k = √(I/M). SI unit: m.

(b) Rod from x = 0 to x = 2a. Axis through x = 0.
Cross-sectional area A, linear density λ = ρA.
Total mass M = 2ρAa.

dm = ρA dx

I = ∫₀^(2a) x² ρA dx = ρA[x³/3]₀^(2a) = 8ρAa³/3 = 4Ma²/3

k = √(I/M) = √(4a²/3) = 2a/√3 = 2a√3/3

question:
(a) State Newton's law of cooling and write out the differential equation describing the temperature of the body.

(b) A beaker of water initially at 100°C is allowed to cool in a room maintained at 15°C. After two minutes, the water temperature is 85°C. Find the temperature of the water after four minutes and the time taken for the water to reach 40°C.
modelAnswer:
(a) Newton's Law of Cooling: The rate of change of temperature of a body is directly proportional to the difference between the body's temperature and the surrounding temperature.

dT/dt = -k(T - Tₛ)

where T = body temperature, Tₛ = surrounding temperature, k = positive constant.

Solution: T(t) = Tₛ + (T₀ - Tₛ)e^(-kt)

(b) Tₛ = 15°C, T₀ = 100°C
T(t) = 15 + 85e^(-kt)

T(2) = 85:
85 = 15 + 85e^(-2k)
70 = 85e^(-2k)
e^(-2k) = 14/17
k = (1/2)ln(17/14) ≈ 0.09613 min⁻¹

T(4):
e^(-4k) = (14/17)² = 196/289
T(4) = 15 + 85(196/289) ≈ 72.65°C

Time to reach 40°C:
40 = 15 + 85e^(-kt)
25 = 85e^(-kt)
e^(-kt) = 5/17
t = ln(17/5)/k ≈ 12.73 minutes

question: (b) Differentiate between discrete and continuous random variable.
modelAnswer:
Discrete Random Variable:
Takes countable, distinct values (usually whole numbers).
Examples: Number of heads in 10 tosses; number of defective items.
Probability assigned to specific values: P(X = x).

Continuous Random Variable:
Takes any value within an interval.
Examples: Height, temperature, time.
Probability described by density function: P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx.
P(X = exact value) = 0.

Key distinction: Discrete RVs are counted; continuous RVs are measured.
